title: The root-sign cone of a split parabolic
statement:
Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a reductive $k$-group [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]: smooth, affine of finite type and geometrically connected, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after algebraic closure. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful finite-dimensional representation. A parabolic $k$-subgroup $P\subseteq G$ is a smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] such that the fppf right-coset sheaf $G/P$ is represented by a proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This sheaf is the sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/P(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras, with $G(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}A,G)$. Write $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}k[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. Let $T\subseteq G$ be a split maximal torus, meaning a closed subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$, $r\geq0$, not strictly contained in another torus, and let $P\subseteq G$ be a parabolic subgroup containing $T$. Put $X^*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-grp}}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and $X_*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-grp}}(\mathbf G_m,T)$, with pointwise multiplication written additively. Define $\langle\alpha,\mu\rangle\in\mathbf Z$ by $\alpha\circ\mu(t)=t^{\langle\alpha,\mu\rangle}$. Let $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ denote the tangent space of $H$ at its identity, with $T$ acting by conjugation, and put $\Phi=\{\alpha\in X^*(T)\setminus\{0\}:\operatorname{Lie}(G)_\alpha\ne0\}$ and $\Phi_P=\{\alpha\in\Phi:\operatorname{Lie}(P)_\alpha\ne0\}$, where the subscript denotes the character-weight space. The set
$$C(P,T)=\{\mu\in X_*(T):\Phi_P=\{\alpha\in\Phi:\langle\alpha,\mu\rangle\geq0\}\}$$
is nonempty. For every $\mu\in X_*(T)$, one has $\mu\in C(P,T)$ if and only if $P=P_\mu$ as subgroup functors on all commutative $k$-algebras, where $P_\mu(A)$ consists of those $g\in G(A)$ for which $t\mapsto\mu(t)g\mu(t)^{-1}$ extends from $\mathbf G_{m,A}$ to an $A$-morphism $\mathbf A^1_A=\operatorname{Spec}A[t]\to G_A$. No algebraic closedness, characteristic or semisimplicity assumption is imposed; $\Phi=\varnothing$ and $P=G$ are allowed.

source.place: Theorem 21.91 and Corollary 21.92, printed pp.453--455; Theorem 25.1, printed p.544, equation (166) and the preceding paragraph. Nonemptiness uses a dominant rational cocharacter on the face indexed by I, multiplied by a positive integer to lie in X_*(T).

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $K/k$. By [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-field-extension], $T_K$ is maximal in $G_K$. It is split. The given geometric hypotheses make $G_K$ reductive and $P_K$ smooth connected; smoothness and properness are preserved by base change by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The sheaf represented by $(G/P)_K$ is $G_K/P_K$: on a $K$-algebra $A$, the cosets and their fppf local lifts are exactly those in the defining quotient over $k$, since every algebra in a covering of $A$ inherits its $K$-structure. Thus $P_K$ is parabolic. By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], the character and cocharacter lattices of the split torus identify across $K/k$, with the same pairing. Tangents and weight spaces also extend scalars: for the augmentation ideal $\mathfrak m$ in a group's coordinate ring, its cotangent space is $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, whose tensor with $K$ is the new cotangent space. A character-weight space is the kernel of $v\mapsto c(v)-v\otimes e_\alpha$ for the conjugation coaction in the Laurent monomial basis of $k[T]$. Tensoring vector spaces with $K$ preserves that kernel and detects nonzero spaces. Consequently $\Phi$ and $\Phi_P$ identify with the corresponding root sets over $K$.

source.place: Theorem 25.1, printed p.544, passage to a splitting field; scalar-extension identifications written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-parabolic-simple-root-exhaustion] to $G_K,T_K,P_K$. Choose its $B$ and write $\Phi^+,\Delta,I$ for the resulting positive roots, simple roots and subset. It gives $\Phi_P=\Phi^+\cup\Phi_I$, with $\Phi_I=\Phi\cap\mathbf Z I$, and $\Delta$ is rationally independent. By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], the integer character-cocharacter pairing is perfect. In particular, if $X=X^*(T_K)$ and $Y=X_*(T_K)$, the rational pairing identifies $Y\otimes\mathbf Q$ with the dual of $X\otimes\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Theorem 21.91 and Proposition 21.90, printed pp.453--454; root datum conventions in Chapter 21.

proof.text: Extend the independent set $\Delta$ to a rational basis of $X\otimes\mathbf Q$. Define a rational functional $f$ to have value $0$ on $I$, value $1$ on $\Delta\setminus I$, and value $0$ on the added basis vectors. By the perfect pairing in step 2 it is pairing with some $q\in Y\otimes\mathbf Q$. Choose $D>0$ clearing the finitely many denominators of $q$ in a lattice basis of $Y$, and put $\mu=Dq\in Y$. For a positive root $\beta=\sum_{\delta\in\Delta}n_\delta\delta$, all $n_\delta\geq0$, and $\langle\beta,\mu\rangle=D\sum_{\delta\notin I}n_\delta$. This vanishes exactly when $\beta\in\Phi_I$ and is otherwise positive. Negating the formula shows that the negative roots with nonnegative pairing are exactly the negative roots in $\Phi_I$. Thus $\{\alpha:\langle\alpha,\mu\rangle\geq0\}=\Phi^+\cup\Phi_I=\Phi_P$. The lattice identification in step 1 makes this an actual cocharacter over $k$. Hence $C(P,T)$ is nonempty. This construction uses a basis of the full character space extending $\Delta$; it does not assume that the roots span that space. If $\Delta$ is empty, choose $f=q=\mu=0$.

source.place: Section 21.i, printed p.452, fundamental rational cocharacters and positive denominator clearing; Theorem 25.1, equation (166), printed p.544.

proof.text:
For an arbitrary $k$-cocharacter $
u$ of $T$, [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry] makes $P_
u$ a smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup and identifies $(P_
u)_K=P_{
u_K}$. The torus $T$ lies in $P_
u$: its elements commute with $
u(t)$ over every test algebra, so the conjugation orbit is constant. Over $K$, [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure] gives $\operatorname{Lie}(P_{
u_K})= igoplus_{n\geq0}\mathfrak g_n$ for the integer weights of $
u$. On the $T_K$-character space $\mathfrak g_\alpha$, this weight is exactly $\langle\alpha,
uangle$, by the definition $\alpha\circ
u(t)=t^{\langle\alpha,
uangle}$. Intersecting the displayed direct sum with each character space therefore gives
$$\Phi_{P_{
u_K}}=\{\alpha\in\Phi:\langle\alpha,
uangle\geq0\}.$$

source.place: Theorem 13.33 and Corollary 21.92, printed p.455; Theorem 25.1, printed p.544.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-overgroup-root-generation] separately to $P_K$ and $P_{
u_K}$; both are smooth connected overgroups of the maximal torus $T_K$, by steps 1 and 4. If $
u\in C(P,T)$, their root sets coincide by step 4. Both subgroup schemes are then the smallest closed subgroup containing the same torus and exactly the same root subgroups, so they are equal. Conversely, equality of these subgroup schemes makes their tangent spaces and character-weight sets equal, and step 4 gives $
u\in C(P,T)$. This uses scheme-theoretic root generation, rather than an inference that arbitrary smooth subgroups with equal Lie algebras must coincide.

source.place: Milne 21.66, printed p.444, applied after the root-sign calculation of equation (166), printed p.544.

proof.text:
By the field-extension clause of [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry], $P_{
u_K}=(P_
u)_K$. Equality of the closed subgroup schemes $P_K$ and $(P_
u)_K$ descends to $k$: if $J,J'$ are their defining ideals in $k[G]$, equality after tensoring with $K$ forces both $(J+J')/J$ and $(J+J')/J'$ to vanish, since tensoring a vector space with the nonzero field $K$ detects zero (extend a nonzero vector to a basis). Hence $J=J'$. The reverse implication follows simply by tensoring equal ideals. Equality of representing closed subgroup schemes is equality of their subgroup functors on every commutative $k$-algebra, including nonreduced algebras. Combining this with step 5 proves the required equivalence. If $P=G$, step 3 allows $I=\Delta$ and $\mu=0$; if $\Phi$ is empty the same argument applies, so no exceptional case is excluded.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q143-457c8924c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement and the Milne source places; no fixes are needed. The item statement is unchanged and true (Milne 25.1, eq. (166), p.544, with 21.91-21.92, pp.453-455). Small cases agree: for GL_2 with B, mu=(a,b) is in C iff a>b iff P_mu=B; for G=T, P=G every mu works; for SL_2 with I empty the step-3 denominator D=2 is needed and is present. Step checks: (1) maximal-torus-field-extension (17.82) has no perfectness assumption; proper-base-change gives smoothness and properness after base change; the antiduality node identifies X^* and, by full faithfulness, X_* with the same pairing; weight spaces commute with tensoring by K. (2) borel-pair-structure states the perfect integer pairing. (3) The face construction is correct: for a root beta, <beta,mu> = D times the sum of its non-I coefficients, which is zero iff beta lies in Phi cap ZI. (4) reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry gives P_nu smooth, geometrically connected, closed and compatible with field extension, and T lies in P_nu; cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure gives Lie(P_nu) as the sum of the weight spaces g_n for n>=0, and splitting by characters gives the displayed root set. (5) Root generation applied to P_K and P_{nu_K} gives equality from equal root sets, and the converse holds by comparing tangent weights. (6) Equality descends from K to k by comparing defining ideals. New node lem-sfb-parabolic-simple-root-exhaustion: 17.16 with 17.10 gives B through T inside P; 21.91 with 21.90(a) gives Phi_P = Phi+ union Phi_I; I is unique; the reductive-to-semisimple reduction is on p.452. It contains no cocharacter clause, so it does not restate the item. New node lem-sfb-maximal-torus-overgroup-root-generation: this is Milne 21.66 (p.444) with H containing T. Since g_alpha is one-dimensional, Lie(H)_alpha nonzero means U_alpha lies in H (21.11c), and generation follows from 10.17; the clause allowing a non-smooth J is valid. Not duplicates of standard-parabolic-levi-charts (semisimple only, constructive), semisimple-root-subgroups-generate, smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation, root-subgroup-parametrizations, split-torus-solvable-cocharacter-containment or parabolic-containing-geometric-maximal-torus.
